headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling create the main leakage/compliance risk; Airbyte adds shared-data and downstream trust pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can ingest business data and Firecrawl can fetch and transform web content via API/MCP, so a workflow where Firecrawl output is fed into Airbyte creates a plausible instruction-in-content bridge. Neither profile proves a default parser trusts instructions, so this is not high; uncertainty pushes it above low.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into Airbyte ingestion without sanitization, prompt-like text can traverse the pair.
IF either agent treats fetched content as instructions rather than data, injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Strip instructions from scraped text before ingestion.
Add a content-type allowlist for Airbyte inputs.
Require human review for any web-derived payload before downstream use.
Use a separate staging workspace for Firecrawl outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from Firecrawl to Airbyte records.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, and API keys and also has broad egress. Together, the pair can move sensitive data across external services by default, and Firecrawl’s API-key handling raises the blast radius. The evidence is docs-only, but the leakage pathway is direct enough to rate high.
conditions: IF Airbyte ingests business data that Firecrawl later scrapes or republishes, sensitive fields can leave the original boundary.
IF Firecrawl is configured with live API keys while processing Airbyte-derived content, secrets exposure becomes possible.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any Firecrawl target pages.
Use a redaction step before sending Airbyte data to Firecrawl.
Restrict Firecrawl to non-sensitive domains.
Rotate any API keys used in Firecrawl after testing.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on the Airbyte-to-Firecrawl handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Firecrawl supports multiple instances plus API/CLI/MCP use, so concurrent writes to shared mutable resources are plausible if they target the same downstream systems. Airbyte’s profile does not show filesystem writes, so the stronger high-severity filesystem/git conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API or datastore without locking, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Firecrawl runs multiple instances against the same target while Airbyte syncs the same records, duplication or overwrite races can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate destination namespaces.
Add idempotency keys to shared writes.
Pause one sync while the other runs on the same dataset.
Check for duplicate records after each run.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared mutable targets.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce structured business data that Firecrawl may then scrape, crawl, or interact with, so one agent’s output can become the other’s input. The profiles do not show explicit verification or human-in-the-loop checks, but they also do not prove blind automation into irreversible actions, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is used as authoritative source data for Firecrawl actions, errors can propagate downstream.
IF Firecrawl-generated content is re-imported into Airbyte without validation, bad records can cascade.
mitigations: Validate Airbyte exports before Firecrawl consumes them.
Compare sampled records against source systems.
Require approval for any Firecrawl action based on Airbyte output.
Log and review mismatches after each sync.
requires-engineering: add schema and semantic validation between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, and API keys and is explicitly API/MCP-capable. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if business data or regulated content is scraped, stored, or forwarded through Firecrawl. No profile shows a specific certification gap, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed from Airbyte into Firecrawl, retention and residency obligations may diverge.
IF Firecrawl logs or stores screenshots containing personal data, subject-rights handling may be inconsistent with Airbyte’s handling.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents.
Block regulated datasets from Firecrawl.
Set short retention on Firecrawl artifacts.
Review vendor DPAs and logging settings.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
